answers.assumption_check: Three load-bearing assumptions, all measured standing: (a) sieves/*.json is read only by build_inspector and the two seed probes (cairn/tools/base/probes/the_seed_versus_living_delta.py, gate_parameters_adjust_from_feedback.py), which compare whole records, so new keys change no behaviour; (b) a finding's `values` rides verbatim into the PROVEME refusal line (transitions._build_gate prints json.dumps(f['values'])), so stamping the why there needs no change outside build_inspector; (c) every one of the 43 registered sieves has a docstring stating its reason, so every backfilled why is read from one, never invented.
answers.builder_check: A Haiku builder needs: the record shape (name, band, band_name, dials, why, why_source with kind akien {quote, at} | law {law} | cc_reading {of}); where bands come from for the 8 records that do not exist yet (the_nest()); the scope of the new sieve (build_inspector's own row only, as no_iou_stands and claim_propagates_with_provenance do); where the why is stamped (fire() in inspect(), into values.sieve_why, so transitions.py is not touched); the verbatim-quote rule and its whitespace folding; and that each why is read from that sieve's docstring. All are in the how and decisions.
answers.children: none, because the records, the sieve, the stamp and the proof are one component's change at cairn/machines/build_inspector/
answers.collision_check: Outline 17.11.6 asks for adjudication against the refusing sieve's intention and why; 17.11.6.1 says each sieve carries its why and its source, and that it is never a question to Akien, so this cast opens none. 17.11.5 (every intention carries a why) is the same rule one rung down. The sieves stay deterministic (17.11.6): the new sieve checks presence, shape and verbatim quotes, never the quality of a why. No collision with no_iou_stands: the sieve records are authored JSON it scans, and no why written here says IOU.
answers.falsifier_check: Five clauses: (1) every registered sieve has a record under sieves/ whose name matches, with a non-blank why and a valid why_source; (2) a registered sieve with no record, a blank why, a malformed why_source, an akien quote absent from the sieve's source, or a record naming no registered sieve each reds every_sieve_carries_its_why on build_inspector's row; (3) every finding inspect() returns carries its sieve's why in values.sieve_why; (4) the PROVEME refusal text for a red component carries the refusing sieve's why; (5) a_run_that_fails_to_run_leaves_a_trail reads its runners from the moved file. Horizon: until the sieve record's shape changes.
answers.gates_bound: code-seam: BUILDME entry gate (chart claim, outline check, answered questions), PROVEME build gate (build_inspector sieves over build_inspector, the new one included), PROVED exit gate (verdict artifact, sealed hollow); proved by the tester, feeds back to origin on failure.
answers.missing_check: Not wrapped until now: the shape of runners_leave_trails.json. It is a list of runner rows that a_run_that_fails_to_run_leaves_a_trail reads, not a sieve record, so it leaves sieves/ for cairn/machines/build_inspector/runners_leave_trails.json beside iou_census.json, and sieves/ then holds exactly one record per registered sieve. Also not wrapped: what makes a why_source checkable. An akien quote must appear verbatim (whitespace folded) in the sieve's own source, so a quote cannot be fabricated; a Law must be one of Law 1..10 or RULE 1; a CC reading must name what it read.
